LibreLane support in basics-graphics-music: suggestions

A review of the ASIC flow scripts 00_setup_libre_lane, 07_synthesize_for_asic, 08_visualize_asic_synthesis_results_1 and 09_visualize_asic_synthesis_results_2 on main. It is based on the code, on LibreLane's documentation and source, and on a check of all 111 labs with the first two stages of the flow.

Summary Update Beginner setup TODO The scripts today The check Fix first Chip contents Configuration Results and setup Later Per-lab results Sources Appendix

Summary

0 of 111labs pass lint or synthesis today
20labs are hidden from LibreLane's lint by `ifndef SIMULATION
25graphics, sound and UART labs synthesize to no logic
92 of 111pass lint and synthesis with the proposed fixes
  1. The ASIC flow has been broken for every lab since 26 July 2026. Commit 136ebf4f made labs/common/config.svh include define_gowin_or_nothing.svh from peripherals/. Script 07 copies five files from labs/common and nothing from peripherals/, so every run stops at the first `include. The fix is one line. The better fix is to stop copying and read the sources in place, as the open-source FPGA flow on main already does (S1).
  2. LibreLane's first step treats the labs as simulation code. LibreLane runs Verilator lint first, Verilator defines VERILATOR, and config.svh then defines SIMULATION. Twenty labs hide lab_top under `ifndef SIMULATION, so lint finds no lab_top and the flow stops. A three-line change to config.svh fixes this (S2).
  3. Graphics and sound labs come out empty. asic_top leaves x, y, red, green, blue, mic, sound and the UART unconnected. Synthesis removes everything that only feeds them, so 25 labs would be hardened as an empty die (S6).
  4. The migration from OpenLane dropped the results students look at. The OpenLane version copied the netlists, timing, power and SDF reports into the lab's run directory and kept a log. The LibreLane version prints a path to librelane_designs/<lab>, and 08 and 09 exit without a message when 07 has not been run (S5, S13).
  5. The configuration uses a deprecated format. LibreLane's source says “Support for .tcl configuration files is deprecated.” Two variable names in it are deprecated, and one file sets the PDK in a way that can only block choosing another (S10). A 40-second regression test would have caught the July break (S16).

Update: the AppImage flow is implemented

After prompt 3, branch claude_libre_lane has an AppImage flow that needs no LibreLane shell opened first. Nothing is committed yet.

What changed

  • 00_setup_libre_lane.source_bash runs LibreLane in one of three ways:
    • librelane in PATH, as before;
    • the AppImage, started by the scripts as <AppImage> librelane <arguments>;
    • the same AppImage under bwrap, when the system disables unprivileged user namespaces and has bwrap installed setuid root.
    The AppImage is $LIBRELANE_APPIMAGE, or the newest librelane*<machine>*.AppImage in the home directory or in ~/Downloads.
  • The code of 07 is now the function librelane_synthesize_for_asic in the same file, and 07 only calls it. On the way it:
    • takes the design directory from $package_dir, as 08 and 09 do, instead of git rev-parse;
    • copies define_gowin_or_nothing.svh (the stopgap of S1), without which no lab works;
    • quotes its paths;
    • protects its rm -rf with ${design_dir:?}.
  • 08 and 09 stop with a clear message when 07 has not been run. They use the flow names OpenInOpenROAD and OpenInKLayout.
  • Documentation: a new docs/LibreLane.md, a LibreLane section in scripts/steps/README.md, and a short “ASIC synthesis” section in README.md.

What I found while doing it

  • How the AppImage takes commands. LibreLane builds it with nix bundle and the ralismark/nix-appimage bundler from its development shell. Its entrypoint runs the command given as arguments inside that environment with exec, so the command's exit status comes back unchanged. Without arguments it opens a shell. LibreLane's own CI runs librelane-devshell-x86_64.AppImage librelane --smoke-test.
  • It needs unprivileged user namespaces. Every program in it is built by Nix with absolute /nix/store/… paths: openroad asks for the loader /nix/store/…-glibc-2.40-66/lib/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, and the yosys wrapper starts with #! /nix/store/…-bash-5.3p3/bin/bash. The AppImage makes its own store appear at /nix in a private mount namespace, which an ordinary user can create only through a user namespace. This machine runs Simply Linux 10.4 (ALT), with kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone = 0. The AppImage stops there with “cannot unshare: Operation not permitted”. ALT installs bwrap setuid root, so the scripts mount the AppImage with FUSE and run its /nix under bwrap, with no root needed.
  • The unpacked tools take 4.9 GB (the AppImage's /nix/store). The AppImage file is 1.4 GB and runs without being unpacked.

Update 2: a setup for a naive user

Prompts 4 to 7 asked why the scripts need bwrap and how they behave on other systems, then asked for a complete shrink-wrapped solution for a naive user. Branch claude_libre_lane now has it. Nothing is committed yet.

Answers to prompts 4 to 6

  • Why bwrap: the AppImage's programs look for their files under /nix/store. The AppImage makes its store appear there with a user namespace, which this machine disables. Setuid bwrap can do the same without them. See Update.
  • bwrap runs only when needed. The scripts try, in order: librelane in PATH, then the AppImage by itself (a test start with true), then bwrap. Choosing takes 0.01 s with librelane in PATH. It takes 0.25 s on this machine, where the direct start fails and the bwrap test start works.
  • Without an AppImage, any installation that puts librelane in PATH works, for example a Nix shell. I tested this inside the AppImage's own environment, which looks to the scripts like a Nix shell. They chose librelane from PATH and ran librelane --version.
  • Windows, macOS and Lubuntu: see the table below.

What a beginner sees on each system

SystemWhat happensTested here
Linux that allows the namespaces: Debian 11 and newer, Fedora, Ubuntu 22.04, Linux Mint 21 The first run of 07 asks Download LibreLane now? [Y/n]. Then it downloads the 3.0.17 AppImage into the home directory and checks its size and SHA-256 sum. The scripts start it for every run. Download, check and resume: yes, with the real file. Direct start: only with a stub, because this machine disables the namespaces.
ALT Linux (this machine) The same, then the AppImage runs under bwrap. Yes: two full runs, the viewers in offscreen mode, Ctrl-C.
Ubuntu 24.04 and newer, and Lubuntu, Kubuntu, Xubuntu and Linux Mint 22 based on it AppArmor stops the AppImage, and bwrap is not setuid there. The script prints LibreLane's two commands (install uidmap, set kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 0) and stops. As you chose, it doesn't run them. The message, with the kernel setting faked.
Windows, Git Bash The script runs itself again in WSL2: wsl.exe --cd <lab> -e bash ./<script>. From there it works as on Linux. Before that, it checks for:
  • no WSL;
  • WSL 1;
  • Windows line endings in the scripts.
For each, it prints the fix.		 Only with stand-ins for wsl.exe and cygpath: the four messages and the exact wsl.exe arguments.
macOS The script prints the Nix steps of LibreLane's guide and stops. After those steps, librelane is in PATH inside nix-shell, and the scripts use it. The message only.

What changed

  • Download (librelane_download_appimage):
    • the version is pinned to librelane_version=3.0.17, with the size and SHA-256 sum of the x86-64 and ARM64 files from the GitHub release;
    • it checks for 4 GB of free space before asking;
    • the prompt is printed with printf, because read -p shows nothing when the input is not a terminal, as under WSL started from Git Bash;
    • it downloads into a .part file with curl -C - (or wget -c), so a later run continues a stopped download.
  • Finding the reason a start fails (librelane_explain_appimage_failure): no FUSE, no /dev/fuse, the AppArmor restriction, kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone = 0 or user.max_user_namespaces = 0. Each gets its own command. Anything else prints the AppImage's whole output.
  • Windows (librelane_run_in_wsl) and macOS (librelane_explain_macos), as in the table.
  • Viewers:
    • 08 and 09 check for results before setting up LibreLane, so running 09 before 07 doesn't offer a 1.4 GB download;
    • on Linux, they stop with a message when there is no display.
  • 07 says how long the flow takes before it starts.
  • Documentation:
    • docs/LibreLane.md has “On Linux”, “On Windows” and “On macOS” sections and a list of what to do when the AppImage cannot start;
    • scripts/steps/README.md lists the 11 setup steps;
    • README.md says the script downloads LibreLane.

What the scripts do today

The scripts were moved from OpenLane 1 to LibreLane in April 2026 (commits fba97686 to cc0f7733) and shortened in April and May (f7a5eafe, f8373f72). 111 directories have the 07_synthesize_for_asic.bash wrapper: 96 in labs, 13 in book and 2 in misc/review_for_style.

FileWhat it does
scripts/steps/00_setup_libre_lane.source_bash For scripts with asic in the name: adds $LIBRELANE_PATH to PATH and stops if there is no librelane command. run_librelane_layout_viewer runs librelane --last-run --flow openin$viewer ./config.tcl in $package_dir/librelane_designs/$lab_name.

It copies asic_top.sv, five files of labs/common, and every .sv .svh .v .vh .hex file of the lab except tb.sv, flattened into src/. It assembles program.s with RARS, then runs librelane --flow Classic config.tcl.

Leftovers 00_setup_open_lane.source_bash and scripts/asic/run_layout_viewer.mk are no longer used. 01_clean still deletes $openlane_dir/designs/$lab_name, a variable nothing sets now.

What I checked, and how

At the time of prompt 1, LibreLane and the sky130 PDK were not installed on this machine, and the disk had 15 GB free, so I did not run the full flow; the Update has a real run. The first two stages decide most of the problems above, and they use tools that are installed here. They are LibreLane's Verilator.Lint step and its Yosys.Synthesis step. I ran them on every lab with the flags LibreLane's source uses:

  • Verilator: verilator --lint-only --Wall --Wno-fatal --relative-includes --Werror-LATCH --Werror-MULTIDRIVEN --top-module asic_top, with the defines PDK_sky130A, SCL_sky130_fd_sc_hd, __librelane__ and __pnr__ (from librelane/steps/verilator.py).
  • Yosys: read_verilog -defer -noautowire -sv with the same defines (from librelane/scripts/pyosys/ys_common.py), or read_slang --top asic_top when USE_SLANG is set. Then synth -flatten and stat. This is generic synthesis without the sky130 library, so the cell counts are Yosys cells, not sky130 cells.

The tools were Verilator 5.053 and Yosys 0.69 with yosys-slang, from OSS CAD Suite. Both variants A and B took 41 seconds for all 111 labs.

A. TodayExactly what 07 copies00

In variant D, 92 labs pass both. The other 19 need changes to the lab or its asic_top, listed in Per-lab results. The scripts and CSV files are in ~/claude/libre_lane/asic_check/. Variant D reads a copy of the sources with the config.svh change from S2 applied.

1. Fix what is broken

S1. Read the sources in place instead of copying a hand-picked subset

Fix firstSmall

Problem. 07_synthesize_for_asic.source_bash:23-46 copies asic_top.sv, five named files of labs/common and the lab's files into one flat src/. This breaks in five ways:

  • config.svh includes define_gowin_or_nothing.svh, which is in peripherals/ and never copied. All 111 labs fail. In 108 the first error is Yosys's “Can't open include file `define_gowin_or_nothing.svh'”.
  • convert, pulse_extender, pulse_on_0_to_1, pulse_to_level and led_strip_combo from labs/common are not copied. Labs 3_11, 3_12, 5_4_yrv and 5_4_1 use them.
  • Modules in peripherals/ are not copied: slow_clk_gen (6_2) and inmp441_mic_i2s_receiver_alt (3_12).
  • Flattening breaks includes with a directory, such as `include "cpu/yrv_mcu.vh" (5_4_yrv, 5_4_1) and sd/sd_controller.vh (99_03).
  • Files with the same name in different subdirectories overwrite each other. In 8_1_uart these are lab_top.sv, uart_pkg.sv and uart_receiver.sv from its three sub-labs.

Proposal. Give LibreLane absolute paths and include directories, the way setup_run_directory_for_fpga_synthesis_yosys in 00_setup_yosys.source_bash already does for the open-source FPGA flow. That means the lab's own tree without run/ and tb.sv, all of labs/common/*.sv and all of peripherals/*.sv, with VERILOG_INCLUDE_DIRS set to the lab, labs/common and peripherals. Unused modules cost nothing, because synthesis starts from asic_top. Two details came out of the check:

  • Stop the walk at subdirectories that are labs themselves, meaning they have their own 07_synthesize_for_asic.bash. Otherwise 8_1_uart reads its three sub-labs at once. The FPGA flow's find has the same problem.
  • Read the lab's filelist.f first, as xilinx_vivado_synthesize.tcl does. Verilator needs packages before their users, and 5_5_aps lists them there.

If a quick stopgap is wanted before that, add one line after 07_synthesize_for_asic.source_bash:33:

cp -f "$peripheral_dir/define_gowin_or_nothing.svh" "$design_dir/src"

S2. Let Verilator lint see the synthesis view of the labs

Fix firstSmall

Problem. LibreLane's first step is Verilator.Lint, and Checker.LintErrors stops the flow on any lint error (ERROR_ON_LINTER_ERRORS is true by default). Verilator defines VERILATOR, which config.svh treats as a simulator, so it defines SIMULATION. Twenty labs wrap lab_top in `ifndef SIMULATION: all of 4_2_fifo, all of 4_3_pipelines_2, 7_1, 7_2 and 9_5. For them, lint reports “Cannot find file containing module: 'lab_top'”. These are the microarchitecture labs, the ones an ASIC timing report is most useful for.

Proposal. LibreLane defines __librelane__ for both lint and synthesis. Check it first in config.svh:

`ifdef __librelane__
    // LibreLane: Verilator lint and Yosys synthesis
    `define NO_SIMULATION
`elsif VCS
    // Synopsys VCS
…

With this change, 19 of the 20 labs pass lint in variant D. The twentieth, 4_2_12, then shows a real error of its own: two drivers on led[1]. Adding LINTER_DEFINES to the configuration would not help, because VERILATOR stays defined either way.

S3. Use the slang frontend, as the open-source FPGA flow already does

Fix firstSmall

Problem. By default LibreLane reads with read_verilog -defer -noautowire -sv. With the include fixed (variant B), Yosys's built-in parser still rejects several labs:

  • break (1_04);
  • function [7:0] f (logic valid, ready) (4_2_7, 4_2_8);
  • import uart_pkg::*; in a module header (8_1_1, 8_1_2, 8_1_3);
  • packages in 5_5_aps;
  • test benches not named tb.sv, which 07 copies (book/05, 7_1, 7_2).

-noautowire also rejects the undeclared counter in 9_events/2024_10_18_maker_faire/8_control_using_keys/lab_top.sv:146. That one is a real bug in the lab.

Proposal. Set USE_SLANG to true. main moved the open-source FPGA flow to read_slang in pull request #343, so both flows would then parse the labs the same way. In variant C, slang fixes 11 labs. It is stricter in two ways, and those failures point to real problems in the labs:

  • Use before declaration (silence in 3_4, quant_cnt_ff in 3_5_3, muxed_clk in 99_03). Fix the labs, or pass slang's --allow-use-before-declare through SLANG_ARGUMENTS.
  • Constant selects out of range on gpio, which is [-1:0] because asic_top sets w_gpio to 0. This affects 3_9, 3_12, 6_1, the Tang Nano 9K copy of 6_1, and 6_2. Give asic_top a w_gpio the labs can index, or guard the gpio uses in the labs. 4_2_12 selects led[11] with 8 LEDs.

S4. Repair or remove the lab copies of the ASIC files

Fix firstSmall

Problem. The lab copies have drifted from the generic files:

  • 5_1_schoolriscv/asic_top.sv:49-50 still connects .vsync and .hsync. These were removed from lab_top and commented out in the generic copy (701b1231).
  • 5_2_schoolriscv_cache/asic_top.sv:29 instantiates a module top, but the lab's module is lab_top.
  • 5_6_hh_single_cycle has asic_top.sv and asic_config.tcl but no 07, 08 or 09 scripts.
  • The three asic_config.tcl files are full copies of config.tcl with a smaller die. They have already drifted: they lack the generic copy's ERROR_ON_LINTER_WARNINGS line.
  • 99_01_camera has a different lab_top interface (no slow_clk, key or w_key), but it has the ASIC scripts.

Proposal. Delete the lab copies of asic_top.sv; the generic one fits both labs. With it, in the variant D setup, 5_1 passes lint and synthesis (3,351 cells). 5_2 passes lint, and slang then reports init_im_req used before its declaration in sr_soc.sv. Replace each full asic_config.tcl with a small override file that holds only what differs, for example an asic_config.json with a die size. 07 can merge it, or pass each key with LibreLane's -c KEY=VALUE. Remove the ASIC scripts from labs that cannot use asic_top, or give those labs their own top.

S5. Make 07, 08 and 09 agree on the directory and say what went wrong

Fix firstSmall

  • 07_synthesize_for_asic.source_bash:4 uses git rev-parse --show-toplevel, while 08 and 09 use $package_dir (00_setup_libre_lane.source_bash:65). Outside a Git checkout, such as an unpacked ZIP, 07 stops with a Git error. Use $package_dir in both.
  • run_librelane_layout_viewer does pushd $design_dir &> /dev/null under set -e. When 07 has not been run, 08 and 09 exit without a message. The OpenLane version checked for the design directory, the runs directory and the signoff results, and said which step to rerun. Bring those checks back. LibreLane's equivalent error is “last_run used without any existing runs”.
  • LAYOUT_VIEWER (00_setup_libre_lane.source_bash:58) is never used, because 08 and 09 always pass a viewer. Drop it, or let 08 honor it.
  • The error text at line 45 prints \'nix develop\' with the backslashes, because \' is literal inside double quotes. It also recommends nix develop, which LibreLane's documentation does not use (S15).
  • 01_clean deletes $openlane_dir/designs/$lab_name, which nothing sets now. Make it delete librelane_designs/$lab_name, and have 01_clean_all delete librelane_designs/.
  • Remove 00_setup_open_lane.source_bash, scripts/asic/run_layout_viewer.mk, and the “Open Lane” line in the tool list comment of 00_setup.source_bash:221.
  • Quote $design_dir in mkdir and pushd (07 lines 7 and 58), so that paths with spaces work.

2. Put the lab into the chip

S6. Connect graphics, sound and the UART in asic_top

NextMedium

Problem. scripts/asic/asic_top.sv:46-56 leaves x, y, mic and uart_rx undriven, and red, green, blue, sound, uart_tx and gpio unconnected. Synthesis removes everything that only drives those outputs. In variant D, 25 labs synthesize to at most one cell for this reason:

  • 9 labs in 2_graphics (all except 2_8);
  • 9 labs in 3_music;
  • book/03 (both copies) and book/11;
  • maker faire labs 1 to 3;
  • 8_1_2_uart_echo.

LibreLane would harden an empty die and report success. In the labs that keep some logic, such as 3_11, what remains is mostly the seven-segment display.

Proposal. Do in asic_top what the FPGA board tops do:

  • Instantiate peripherals/vga.sv to drive x and y.
  • Bring out hsync and vsync and two bits per color, gated by display_on. Two bits per color is the TinyVGA Pmod that BGM already supports, and the Tiny Tapeout convention (S17).
  • Bring sound out through peripherals/audio_pwm.sv as one pin.
  • Bring mic in through the INMP441 receiver as three pins.
  • Bring out uart_rx and uart_tx.

That is about a dozen pins on top of today's 39.

    wire display_on;

    vga # (.CLK_MHZ (clk_mhz), .PIXEL_MHZ (25)) i_vga
    (
        .clk        ( clk        ),
        .rst        ( rst        ),
        .hsync      ( vga_hsync  ),
        .vsync      ( vga_vsync  ),
        .display_on ( display_on ),
        .hpos       ( x          ),
        .vpos       ( y          ),
        .pixel_clk  (            )
    );

    assign vga_r = display_on ? red   [w_red   - 1 -: 2] : '0;
    assign vga_g = display_on ? green [w_green - 1 -: 2] : '0;
    assign vga_b = display_on ? blue  [w_blue  - 1 -: 2] : '0;

S7. Constrain the clocks the way the lab is built

NextSmall

  • CLOCK_PERIOD is 14 ns (71.4 MHz), but asic_top gives the lab clk_mhz = 50, which is 20 ns. The lab's counters and strobes assume one clock and timing analysis checks another. Derive one from the other: pass clk_mhz with SYNTH_PARAMETERS, which LibreLane passes to slang as -G, and set CLOCK_PERIOD to 1000 / clk_mhz.
  • slow_clk is a pin, but only clk is in CLOCK_PORT, so flip-flops on slow_clk are not timed. On FPGA boards, 63 of 115 board tops make slow_clk from clk with peripherals/slow_clk_gen.sv. Do the same in asic_top with a generated clock in the SDC. The simpler alternative is to list both pins in CLOCK_PORT.
  • Let a student try other periods without editing files, by passing the 07 arguments to LibreLane: ./07_synthesize_for_asic.bash -c CLOCK_PERIOD=8. The misc/caravel notes give learning to balance microarchitecture, area and timing as the reason for the ASIC flow. The pipeline labs (4_1, 4_3) are where that shows.

S8. Size the die from the design

NextSmall

Every lab gets an absolute 1000 × 1000 µm die (500 × 500 for the three CPU copies). That is 1 mm² for one XOR gate in 1_01, and for about 3,100 cells in 4_1_1. 5_5_aps has about 69,500 Yosys cells and may need more. LibreLane's default is FP_SIZING: relative with FP_CORE_UTIL (50 by default), which sizes the die from the synthesized area. Use it, and keep an absolute DIE_AREA only as a per-lab override. Smaller dies route faster and give pictures in which the cells can be seen.

S9. Decide what to do with memories

LaterMedium

5_3_picorv32 synthesizes to about 35,000 Yosys cells, almost 10,000 of them flip-flops, because its instruction memory becomes flip-flops. 5_5_aps is about 69,500 cells. There are two options. One is a smaller memory under `ifdef __librelane__. The other is a RAM macro through LibreLane's MACROS variable. The misc/caravel notes already mention OpenLane's problems with memory inference.

3. Modernize the configuration

S10. Generate a JSON configuration instead of copying Tcl

NextMedium

  • Deprecated format. LibreLane's config.py warns: “Support for .tcl configuration files is deprecated. Please migrate to a .json file at your earliest convenience.” The migration guide calls Tcl “finicky”.
  • Old names. SYNTH_MAX_FANOUT is now a deprecated name of MAX_FANOUT_CONSTRAINT, a PDK variable. PL_TARGET_DENSITY is a deprecated name of PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT, which is in percent; LibreLane multiplies the old value by 100. If it is not set, LibreLane uses FP_CORE_UTIL + 5 × GPL_CELL_PADDING + 10. ERROR_ON_LINTER_WARNINGS 0 is already the default.
  • The PDK line. sky130A_sky130_fd_sc_hd_config.tcl:3 sets ::env(PDK) to sky130A (7b70f50c, “explicitly define PDK”). The file is sourced only when the PDK is already sky130A (config.tcl:11). In LibreLane a PDK set in the configuration wins over --pdk, so the line can do nothing except block another PDK. Remove it, and use "pdk::sky130*" sections for PDK-specific values.

With S1, 07 has the file list anyway, so it can write config.json next to the run. For 1_06_binary_counter it would look like this, with paths shortened:

{
  "meta": { "version": 2, "flow": "Classic" },

  "DESIGN_NAME": "asic_top",

  "VERILOG_FILES": [
    "…/scripts/asic/asic_top.sv",
    "…/labs/1_basics/1_06_binary_counter/lab_top.sv",
    "…/labs/common/counter_with_enable.sv",
    "…  the rest of labs/common/*.sv and peripherals/*.sv"
  ],

  "VERILOG_INCLUDE_DIRS": [
    "…/labs/1_basics/1_06_binary_counter",
    "…/labs/common",
    "…/peripherals"
  ],

  "USE_SLANG": true,
  "SYNTH_PARAMETERS": [ "clk_mhz=50" ],

  "CLOCK_PORT": "clk",
  "CLOCK_PERIOD": 20,

  "FP_SIZING": "relative",
  "FP_CORE_UTIL": 40,

  "pdk::sky130*": {
    "MAX_FANOUT_CONSTRAINT": 6
  }
}

S11. Let the student choose the PDK

LaterSmall

LibreLane 3.0 added KLayout DRC for gf180mcu and the IHP PDKs (ihp-sg13g2, ihp-sg13cmos5l), next to sky130A. Tiny Tapeout runs shuttles on SkyWater, GlobalFoundries and IHP processes. A variable such as BGM_ASIC_PDK passed as --pdk would let a class harden the same lab at 130 nm and 180 nm and compare area and speed. PDK-specific values go into "pdk::…" sections.

S12. Name the runs and keep the directory small

NextSmall

Without --run-tag, each run creates a new runs/RUN_<date>_<time>, and nothing deletes them. Use a fixed tag with --overwrite, for example --run-tag bgm --overwrite, so a lab has one run. Then 08 and 09 can use --run-tag bgm instead of --last-run. A student who wants to compare two clock periods can pass another tag.

4. Give students readable results and an easier setup

S13. Copy the results into the lab's run directory and print a summary

NextMedium

The OpenLane version copied 11 files into run. They were the synthesis, placement, routing and final netlists, the setup, hold and power reports, LEF, Magic and SDF, named asic_02_synthesis.v to asic_12_standard_delay_format.sdf. It also kept the log with tee. fba97686 removed all of that. LibreLane has what is needed to bring it back:

  • --save-views-to run/asic_views copies the final views, such as netlists, layout and timing files. The help text says: “A directory to copy the final views to”.
  • runs/<tag>/final/metrics.csv and metrics.json hold the flow's metrics, such as area, cell counts, slack, power and the DRC, LVS and antenna counts. 07 can print five or six lines from them at the end: die area, cells, worst setup and hold slack, maximum frequency, power, and violations.
  • The KLayout.Render step writes asic_top.png, a picture of the layout, into its step directory. Copying it to run/ gives students a picture without a GUI. That helps under WSL and Docker, and when 08 or 09 cannot open a window.
  • Pipe the LibreLane output through tee "$log" as the other steps do. --condensed keeps it short.

S14. A quick mode for timing and area

NextSmall

The Classic flow has about 80 steps, and the signoff steps take most of the time. For the microarchitecture labs, a student usually wants the area and the critical path before placement and routing. --to OpenROAD.STAPrePNR stops after synthesis and pre-layout timing. Offer it as a variable or a separate script. A small table of the 4_1 and 4_3 labs would be a good classroom exercise: area and maximum frequency of the single-cycle and pipelined versions side by side. In the generic synthesis above, 4_1_1 has 3,104 cells and 4_1_2 has 3,472.

S15. Detect the installation and point to the easy one

AppImage part implementedSmall

  • LibreLane's installation page lists Nix as best, the AppImage as easiest and Docker as the fallback. The AppImage is one file, librelane-devshell-x86_64.AppImage, with no Docker. Running it opens a shell with librelane on the path. That suits the misc/caravel notes, which find Docker an extra hassle. With Nix, the docs clone the repository and run nix-shell, not nix develop. Put these three ways in the error message and in a new docs/LibreLane.md, next to docs/Yosys.md.
  • Support Docker without a separate setup, with a variable such as LIBRELANE_DOCKERIZED=1 that turns librelane into python3 -m librelane --dockerized. --dockerized must come first. It mounts the home directory, the PDK root and the current directory. A BGM checkout outside the home directory needs --docker-mount. 08 and 09 need a display inside the container, which LibreLane's pages do not describe; the PNG from S13 is the fallback.
  • Say plainly that Git Bash on Windows is not enough: LibreLane needs WSL2 or Docker. On macOS it runs with Nix or Docker.
  • Warn about disk space and the first-run download. Measured for LibreLane 3.0.17 on 20 November 2026:
    • the AppImage is one 1.4 GB file;
    • the Docker image is a 1.5 GB download that unpacks to about 5.8 GB. A Nix installation probably holds about the same, since the image is built from the same Nix packages;
    • the first run downloads the default sky130 libraries into ~/.ciel, a 0.34 GB download that unpacks to 2.2 GB. The gf180mcu default set is a 0.58 GB download, and IHP sg13g2 is 0.41 GB.
    That is about 4 GB with the AppImage and about 8 GB with Docker or Nix, before any runs. The size of a run was not measured, and runs pile up without S12. For events with prepared machines, such as the bootable SSDs in the misc/caravel notes, run librelane --smoke-test once before copying, so that the PDK is already there.
  • Check librelane --version. Version 3.0 removed the openlane command and renamed variables. The latest stable release is 3.0.17 (26 October 2026); Tiny Tapeout's local hardening guide pins 3.0.14.

S16. Add a regression test for the ASIC sources

Fix firstSmall

The July break went unnoticed for four months. The check in this report needs only Verilator and Yosys from OSS CAD Suite, with no PDK and no LibreLane. It runs the two first steps on all 111 labs in about 40 seconds. Put a version of it in scripts/tests/ with a list of the labs that are expected to fail, and run it in CI. Tiny Tapeout's templates show that the full flow also runs in GitHub Actions (tt-gds-action). One or two small labs hardened there would cover the rest of the flow.

5. Later: from layout to silicon

S17. A Tiny Tapeout wrapper for the labs

LaterLarge

Tiny Tapeout hardens user projects with LibreLane. Its top module has ui_in[7:0], uo_out[7:0], uio_in, uio_out, uio_oe (8 bits each), ena, clk and rst_n. A tile is about 167 × 108 µm, and a project can use 1×1 up to 8×2 tiles. Its VGA convention is the TinyVGA Pmod: uo_out = {hsync, B0, G0, R0, vsync, B1, G1, R1}, with audio on uio_out[7]. A tt_um_bgm_* wrapper could map:

  • ui_in to keys and switches;
  • uo_out to TinyVGA;
  • uio_out[7] to sound;
  • three uio pins to a TM1638 board, which already gives BGM labs their LEDs, digits and keys on boards without them.

The same lab would then drive the same Pmods on an FPGA board and on a Tiny Tapeout chip. The local hardening commands are ./tt/tt_tool.py --pdk $PDK --create-user-config and ./tt/tt_tool.py --pdk $PDK --harden. The misc/caravel notes mention an earlier template for Verilog Meetup, tt10-verilog-template-for-verilog-meetup, which could be the starting point.

S18. One chip for a group

LaterLarge

The misc/caravel notes describe a class building one larger chip together, on Caravel-Mini. Efabless, which ran Caravel, closed in 2025. wafer.space now sells GF180MCU shuttle slots for this kind of project, using LibreLane's new Chip flow and a pad-ring template (gf180mcu-project-template). It would need its own top with many labs behind a selector. That is a project of its own, but the generated configuration from S10 is a step toward it.

S19. Simulate the netlist with the lab's own testbench

LaterMedium

Most labs have tb.sv, and LibreLane writes the final netlist into final/nl and final/pnl. Running the same testbench on the netlist with Icarus and the PDK's cell models shows what gate-level simulation is, at little cost. Tiny Tapeout's template does the same with its gl_test job.

S20. Put FPGA and ASIC numbers side by side

LaterSmall

BGM already reports LUTs, registers and timing for FPGA builds. With the summary from S13, a per-lab table of FPGA LUTs and Fmax against ASIC area and Fmax would show where the two technologies differ. That is the point the misc/caravel notes make about FPGA timing not being ASIC timing.

Suggested order

  1. S1 stopgap line, S2 and S5. They are small, and the flow works again for most labs.
  2. S16, so that it stays working.
  3. S1 in full, S3, S4 and S10 together, because they all change how 07 builds the configuration.
  4. S6, S7, S8, S12 and S13, the changes that make the result worth looking at.
  5. S14 and S15, then the later items as the course needs them.
